chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Abu Ishaq Tha'labah, from Zurarah, from one of the two Imams, meaning Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them), who said:
Allah, the Mighty and High, has not been served by anything like the Appearance (Al-Bada').

key_terms.أَحَدِهِمَا: One of the two, referring to either Imam al-Baqir or Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon them).
key_terms.الْبَدَاءِ: Al-Bada' (The Appearance/Manifestation), a theological concept referring to the manifestation of a divine decree that was previously hidden or unknown to creation.
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Azza wa Jalla (The Mighty and High), an honorific title for Allah.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Al-Bada' in Shia theology and how does it relate to worship?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Tawhid*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates *Al-Bada’*—the divine manifestation of a decree to suit changing circumstances—not merely as a theological concept, but as the pinnacle of worship (*‘ibadah*). This reflects the Shia scholarly view that recognizing God’s absolute sovereignty over time and fate, beyond fixed destiny, constitutes a profound act of devotion. It underscores the dynamic nature of divine will, where knowledge of *Al-Bada’* deepens the believer’s connection to Allah’s wisdom.
